description.value: Hike-in backcountry campground set in subalpine meadows beneath the iconic Black Tusk in Garibaldi Park; spectacular alpine terrain but trail access only means a loaded touring bike stays at the Rubble Creek trailhead.

address.value: Unnamed Road, 0A0,, Whistler, BC V8E 0C2, Canada

enrichment_extras.reasoning: Taylor Meadows Campground is confirmed as a real backcountry campground within Garibaldi Provincial Park — the BC Parks website explicitly names it under the 'Black Tusk/Garibaldi Lake' area section. The OSM-discovered URL (bcparks.ca/garibaldi-park/) matches the live website, and the park clearly operates an active reservation system ('Book camping' including backcountry). However, the website provides no amenity specifics for Taylor Meadows itself, cycling access to the backcountry campground is unconfirmed, and the park explicitly prohibits motorized 'trail bikes' in backcountry areas while not addressing non-motorized bicycle access.
concerns: Website covers Garibaldi Park overall; no amenity details specific to Taylor Meadows Campground are provided.
Bicycle access to Taylor Meadows is unconfirmed — park explicitly prohibits motorized 'trail bikes' in backcountry; non-motorized cycling access not addressed.
No address or phone number available for this campground in OSM or on the website.
Backcountry wilderness campground requiring significant trail travel to reach; may not be accessible to standard road or gravel touring cyclists.
Dogs and all pets (except certified service animals per IGDF/ADI) are explicitly prohibited in the park.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Taylor Meadows is a legitimate and active backcountry campground in a world-class provincial park, but cycling access is unconfirmed — the park prohibits motorized trail bikes in backcountry and the website does not address non-motorized bicycle access to Taylor Meadows. Suitability for the WWC cycling directory depends on whether bike access to the campground is permitted.
enrichment_extras.notes: BC Parks general contact: 1-800-689-9025 (toll-free Canada/US) / parkinfo@gov.bc.ca. Fires are explicitly prohibited in Garibaldi Park. The backcountry is described as demanding and visitors must be fully self-sufficient. Day-use passes are required for Garibaldi Park visits.
